note: Dak Prescott is the QB8 in fantasy points per game. He has at least 23.3 fantasy points in two games this season, and he has scored at least 19.5 fantasy points in each of his last three games. Among 31 qualifying passers, he is 16th in yards per attempt, 14th in passing success rate, fourth in highly accurate throw rate, and ninth in hero throw rate. Prescott could keep the good times rolling this week, but I'm worried that he has a down week. The 49ers' pass defense has been formidable. Over their last five games, San Francisco has allowed the ninth-fewest yards per attempt, the tenth-lowest passing success rate, the eighth-lowest EPA per dropback, and the 13th-lowest fantasy points per dropback.

Patrick Mahomes is the QB15 in fantasy points per game, with three games with at least 22 fantasy points. He had a scare last week with his right elbow getting injured. Mahomes is day-to-day. I expect him to play this week, but I wouldn't be surprised if his aDOT is low this week. That wouldn't be a departure from what he has done for most of the season, though. Among 31 qualifying passers, Mahomes is ninth in yards per attempt and third in passing success rate while having the lowest aDOT (5.74) and the most passing yards from yards after the catch (68.3%). Mahomes should turn in another QB1 outing this week. Over their last five games, Atlanta has allowed the tenth-most yards per attempt, the second-highest passing success rate, the 11th-highest passing touchdown rate, and the sixth-highest passer rating.

Tyler Shough has turned around his play with at least 19.7 fantasy points in two of his last three games. Overall, he is QB12 in fantasy points per game. He showed off his wheels last week with ten carries and 51 rushing yards. It was his third game of the season with at least 30 rushing yards. Among 31 qualifying passers, he is 25th in yards per attempt, 18th in passing success rate, tenth in catchable target rate, and sixth in hero throw rate. Shough should continue to motor along as a QB1 this week. Over their last five games, Carolina has allowed the 11th-highest passing success rate, the eighth-highest CPOE, and the ninth-most EPA per dropback.

The last time that Jayden Daniels faced this defense, he was the QB2 in weekly scoring, but that was related more to his 103 rushing yards and two rushing scores than to what he did as a passer. Since his return in Week 5, Daniels has been the QB7 in fantasy points per game, averaging 4.8 rushing attempts and 38 rushing yards. Among 31 qualifying passers, Daniels is 18th in yards per attempt, 22nd in passing success rate, ninth in highly accurate throw rate, and 15th in catchable target rate. Daniels will need all the rushing production he can get this week. The Giants' pass defense has been much improved. Over their last five games, they have allowed the fewest yards per attempt, the lowest passing success rate, the seventh-lowest passer rating, and the fourth-lowest EPA per dropback.

After last week's insane 36.4 fantasy-point outing, C.J. Stroud is the QB6 in fantasy points per game. Stroud is playing the best football of his career. At this point, that's not debatable. Among 31 qualifying passers, he is sixth in yards per attempt, 13th in passing success rate, seventh in highly accurate throw rate, and third in hero throw rate. Stroud has four 300-yard passing days this season while tossing for multiple passing touchdowns in five games. He'll have an uphill climb this week to meet the lofty weekly bar he has set this season. The Browns' pass defense remains one of the best in the league. Over their last five games, they have allowed the third-lowest passing touchdown rate, the eighth-lowest yards per attempt, the third-lowest passing success rate, and the seventh-lowest EPA per dropback.

After last week's shellacking of the Pats, Jordan Love is the QB4 in fantasy points per game. Among 30 qualifying passers, Love is seventh in passing touchdown rate, first in deep ball rate, 21st in catchable target rate, and fourth in hero throw rate. He'll have his work cut out for him this week. Over their last five games, Minnesota has allowed the third-fewest yards per attempt, the second-lowest passing touchdown rate, the 13th-lowest passing success rate, and the fewest fantasy points per dropback. In that span, Minny has also had the highest blitz and pressure rates in the NFL. Love has crushed the blitz, ranking ninth in passer rating, tenth in EPA per dropback, and eighth in passing touchdown rate against it. Love has a wide range of outcomes this week against a formidable foe. He could cook again this week or get cooked if the Vikings' pass rush consistently gets home against the Packers' offensive line.

Bryce Young has course corrected. After flailing as the QB24 and QB18 in Weeks 7 & 8, Young bounced back last week against Denver as the QB6 in fantasy. Overall, he is the QB11 in fantasy points per game. Among 31 qualifying passers, Young is 15th in yards per attempt and passing success rate, 18th in hero throw rate, and 22nd in catchable target rate. Young should continue to ride the comeback train this week. The Saints' pass defense continues to be a weak unit. Over their last five games, New Orleans has allowed the third-most yards per attempt, the 12th-highest passing success rate, the ninth-highest CPOE, and the 13th-most fantasy points per dropback.

Aaron Rodgers is the QB20 in fantasy points per game. He has three games this season with at least 20 fantasy points per game, but he hasn't had one of those outings since Week 5. Among 31 qualifying passers, he is 23rd in yards per attempt and passing success rate, 15th in highly accurate throw rate, 23rd in catchable target rate, and 26th in hero throw rate. Rodgers should check in with solid QB2 numbers this week, but I also wouldn't be shocked if he flirts with low-end QB1 production if Pittsburgh is forced to play catch-up or keep pace with Cincy's high-octane offense. Over their last five games, Cincy has allowed the 14th-most yards per attempt, the eighth-highest passing success rate, the 12th-most EPA per dropback, and the 14th-most fantasy points per dropback.

Matthew Stafford is the QB16 in fantasy points per game, with four games with at least 18.5 fantasy points. Unfortunately for Stafford, his receiving weapons are dropping like flies, with Terrance Ferguson, Davante Adams, and Puka Nacua all hurt. It has also come out that Stafford is dealing with elbow discomfort. This explains his erratic play at times this season. Among 31 qualifying passers, Stafford is 19th in yards per attempt, tenth in passing success rate, 18th in highly accurate throw rate, 20th in catchable target rate, and he has the ninth-highest turnover-worthy throw rate. The Rams have been leaning more run-heavy over their last four games and will likely continue to do so considering all the circumstances. Across his last four games, Stafford has surpassed 33 passing attempts only once. He hasn't surpassed 230 passing yards in any game during that stretch. Despite all of these factors, Stafford could still post decent QB2 numbers this week because Arizona's pass defense has been buns. Over their last five games, Arizona has allowed the ninth-highest passing touchdown rate, the seventh-highest passer rating, the fourth-highest EPA per dropback, and the fourth-highest fantasy points per dropback.

Drew Lock will make another start this week. In his two starts this season, he has been the QB9 and QB19 in weekly scoring. Lock is playing through an oblique and an elbow issue. Among 37 qualifying passers, Lock is tenth in yards per attempt, fourth in passing success rate, second in highly accurate throw rate, 33rd in aDOT, and 27th in hero throw rate. He has been a game manager. Lock could post very good QB2 numbers this week even in that role. Over their last five games, the Raiders have allowed the second-most yards per attempt, the highest passing touchdown rate, the third-highest passing success rate, and the most EPA per dropback.

J.J. McCarthy is good to go this week after picking up a hip pointer last week. His success on the field hasn't equated to fantasy success over the last two games, but that could change this week. Over the last two games, he has scored zero touchdowns, which is holding his fantasy stats down. Washington's pass defense has improved. Over their last five games, Washington has allowed the sixth-lowest passing touchdown rate, the 12th-lowest passing success rate, the ninth-fewest fantasy points per dropback, and the 12th-lowest EPA per dropback. McCarthy is a solid QB2 this week who'll need to continue to be on his A game to be a QB1.

Geno Smith is the QB23 in fantasy points per game with three outings of at least 19 fantasy points. Among 31 qualifying passers, Smith is 11th in yards per attempt, 12th in passing success rate, and eighth in catchable target rate and hero throw rate. Smith has three games with at least 287 passing yards and multiple scores this season. Smith should post decent QB2 numbers this week. The Bills have upgraded to a middle-of-the-road pass defense. Over their last five games, Buffalo has ranked 15th in passing success rate, 18th in passing touchdown rate, and 19th in fantasy points per dropback allowed.

Kirk Cousins returns to familiar territory after the trade to be the Vikings' starting quarterback. I expect him to be under center this week for Minnesota. Cousins is the QB7 in fantasy points per game. Among 30 qualifying passers, he is 12th in yards per attempt, ninth in passing success rate, 24th in catchable target rate, and 22nd in CPOE. Cousins won't have an easy task this week. The Packers' pass defense has been humming. Over their last five games, they have allowed the fifth-fewest yards per attempt, the 11th-lowest passing success rate, the tenth-lowest CPOE, and the fourth-fewest fantasy points per dropback. Cousins will also have to contend with the third-best pressure rate in the NFL over that span. Cousins is best viewed as a mid-range QB2.

Deshaun Watson will retake the starting job for Cleveland this week. Watson is the QB21 in fantasy points per game, averaging 6.4 rushing attempts and 27.1 rushing yards. Among 31 qualifying passers, Watson is 13th in yards per attempt, 11th in passing success rate, eighth in highly accurate throw rate, and 18th in catchable target rate. Watson has absorbed the sixth-highest pressure rate and the 11th-highest quick pressure rate this season, which could be his undoing this week. Houston's pass defense has begun to round into form. Over their last five games, they have allowed the 14th-lowest passing success rate, the 11th-lowest passing touchdown rate, and the 12th-fewest fantasy points per dropback. During that span, they have had the ninth-best pressure rate and are tied for the fifth-most sacks generated. Watson could be under duress all game. He's a low-end QB2.

Jacoby Brissett will provide a bump to the Baltimore offense. We'll see if that happens in his first start, but it's a great matchup. Brissett is the QB24 in fantasy points per game. Among 31 qualifying passers, he is 31st in yards per attempt, 17th in passing success rate, 12th in catchable target rate and highly accurate throw rate, and 28th in hero throw rate. The Bolts' pass defense has fallen apart. Over their last five games, the Chargers have allowed the eighth-most yards per attempt, the fourth-highest passing touchdown rate, the 13th-highest passing success rate, and the seventh-most fantasy points per dropback.

Michael Penix is the QB24 in fantasy points per game. He has been riding the struggle bus over the last two weeks with a combined 16.7 fantasy points. Penix has surpassed 15 fantasy points only twice this season. Among 31 qualifying passers, he is 19th in passing success rate, 31st in deep ball rate, and 27th in highly accurate throw rate and catchable target rate. Among that quarterback sample, he has the highest turnover-worthy throw rate. I don't see him turning things around this week. Penix is a low-end QB2 again. Over their last five games, Kansas City has allowed the seventh-lowest passing touchdown rate, the seventh-lowest passing success rate, and the tenth-lowest passer rating.

Justin Herbert remains off the fantasy radar. He hasn't eclipsed 15 fantasy points in any game this season. It has been a train wreck season for Herbert. He has one passing touchdown and four interceptions in his last three games. He hasn't passed for more than 260 yards in any game. Herbert has an interception in every game this season. Herbert isn't worth starting in any format.

Daniel Jones is the QB37 in fantasy points per game. He hasn't scored at least 16 fantasy points in any game this season. I doubt that will happen this week, either. Keenan Allen is gone. Josh Downs is gone. Tyler Warren is his only receiving threat of major note. Jones has zero games this season with multiple passing touchdowns or at least 270 passing yards. I'm not starting him in any format this week. He couldn't flash a fantasy pulse against Dallas last week, so I doubt it will happen this week.

I know the last time we saw Cam Ward, he had arguably the best game of his NFL career, but he's still tough to trust in fantasy. Ward is still the QB29 in fantasy points per game, with only two games this season with more than 17 fantasy points. Among 31 qualifying passers, Ward is 29th in yards per attempt, 21st in passing success rate, 24th in highly accurate throw rate, and 30th in hero throw rate. He was efficient against Cincy, but it was smoke and mirrors to an extent. That week, Ward had the seventh-lowest aDOT (6.65) and time to throw. 15% of his passing plays were screens. I need to see Ward succeed consistently for a few games before I'm willing to trust him. Sit Ward this week. Over their last five games, the Jags have allowed the 14th-fewest yards per attempt, the ninth-lowest passing success rate, the eighth-lowest CPOE, and have ranked seventh in pressure rate.

With Kirk Cousins in Minnesota now, Fernando Mendoza will assume the starting role with Las Vegas. It will be a trial by fire in his first NFL start against one of the best pass defenses in the NFL. In the preseason, among 62 qualifying quarterbacks, Mendoza was 43rd in yards per attempt, 32nd in adjusted completion rate, and he had zero big-time throws. I'm not expecting much from Mendoza in his first NFL start, especially considering the defense he'll face. Over their last five games, Seattle has allowed the second-fewest yards per attempt, the fourth-lowest passing touchdown rate, and the tenth-lowest passing success rate.

Kyle McCord will start for Miami this week with Malik Willis sidelined with a groin injury. It will be McCord's first NFL start. Let's discuss him as a prospect before we get into this week's outlook. Coming out of Syracuse, among all FBS quarterbacks with at least 150 dropbacks, he ranked 29th in adjusted completion rate, 31st in yards per attempt, and 22nd in big-time throw rate (per PFF). He was a game manager who was at his best when peppering the short and intermediate areas of the field with targets. He has a quick release with average arm strength. We'll see if he can muster decent QB2 numbers this week. Over their last five games, Indy has allowed the second-most yards per attempt, the fourth-highest passing touchdown rate, and the tenth-highest EPA per dropback.

With Jacoby Brissett traded and Gardner Minshew hurt, Carson Beck will assume the starting role for Arizona. Before I get into this game, let's discuss Beck as a prospect entering the league. I like Beck to an extent as a possible career backup who could give you a few starts in a pinch if needed. Beck is at his best when he's gripping and ripping passes to the short and intermediate levels. He can play the role of point guard for a passing attack, but I don't consider him to be a passer that can put on the Superman cape weekly if needed. In his final collegiate season, among all FBS quarterbacks with at least 150 dropbacks (per PFF), he was eighth in adjusted completion rate and 32nd in yards per attempt, but he was also 131st in aDOT and 102nd in big-time throw rate. The Rams are a below-average matchup for Beck. Over their last five games, the Rams have allowed the fifth-lowest passing touchdown rate, the 14th-lowest passer rating, the 14th-lowest fantasy points per dropback, and the tenth-lowest EPA per dropback. Also, add that Beck is flanked by unproven weapons in the receiver room outside of Trey McBride. His first NFL start could be ugly. Sit Beck.

Since Week 5, Ollie Gordon has been the RB22 in fantasy points per game, averaging 20 touches and 80.1 total yards. Among 45 qualifying backs this season, he is tenth in explosive run rate and 21st in missed tackle rate. Gordon should produce another solid volume-based RB2 stat line again this week. Over their last five games, Indy has allowed the eighth-highest rushing success rate, the fifth-most rushing yards over expectation per attempt, and the 11th-highest yards after contact per attempt.

Chase Brown is the RB20 in fantasy points per game as a weekly volume play. He has had horrible touchdown luck, with zero touchdowns since Week 1 and only one score this season. Since Week 5, Brown has averaged 15.8 touches and 73.5 total yards while splitting the early-down work with Samaje Perine. Since Week 5, Brown has had a 66.9% snap rate, a 47.9% rushing share, a 60% route share, and a 15.1% target share. Across his last three games, Brown's efficiency has begun to improve as Cincy's offensive line has gotten their act together. In those games, Brown has had 2.38 yards before contact per attempt, which has allowed him to rip a 13.3% explosive run rate and 2.38 yards after contact per attempt. Just for context, with that small 32-carry sample size. If Brown puts that sample up against all backs with at least 32 carries this season (62 rushers), he'd rank 15th in explosive run rate and 19th in yards after contact per attempt. Brown faces a tough matchup this week, but he should see enough volume to be at least a decent RB2. Over their last five games, the Steelers have allowed the seventh-lowest explosive run rate, the third-lowest rushing success rate, and the fewest yards before contact per attempt.

Last week, in his return, Breece Hall's workload was managed. He was second behind Braelon Allen in snap rate (43.5%) and route share (21.1%), while he led the duo in rushing workload (60% vs. 32%). Hall had a target or touch on 19 of his 27 snaps last week. Hall finished with 18 touches and 87 total yards. Hall had two red zone rushing attempts to Braelon Allen's one. The Jets eased Hall in, and I expect him to take over more of the snaps this week. Hall has posted only 1.68 yards after contact per attempt and a 15% missed tackle rate this season. Hall has another meh matchup this week. He could be a volume-based RB2 this week. Over their last five games, Buffalo has allowed the 13th-lowest rushing success rate and the 11th-lowest yards after contact per attempt while ranking 15th in rushing yards over expectation per attempt and explosive run rate.

Since Week 6, Tony Pollard has been the RB2 in fantasy points per game, averaging 23.7 touches and 122.6 total yards. Among 45 qualifying rushers, Pollard is 17th in explosive run rate, fifth in yards after contact per attempt, and 20th in missed tackle rate. He will face a formidable and new-look Jags run defense this week with the additions of Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux. Pollard will need all the volume he can swallow up this week. The Jags remain an elite run defense. Over their last five games, they have allowed the lowest explosive run rate, the lowest rushing success rate, and the seventh-lowest rushing yards over expectation per attempt.

Last week, Zach Charbonnet took over as Seattle's lead back. He had a 57.4% snap rate, a 48.5% rushing share, and a 44.8% route share (7.1% target share). Charbonnet was the RB22 in weekly scoring with 17 touches and 86 total yards. In his limited action this season, Charbonnet has been impressive with 3.14 yards after contact per attempt and a 27% missed tackle rate. He should have plenty of room to rumble this week. Over their last five games, the Raiders have allowed the fourth-highest explosive run rate, the highest rushing success rate, the 13th-most yards after contact per attempt, and the eighth-highest missed tackle rate.

Woody Marks has been posting hollow bell cow volume. Since Week 6, he has had a 76.5% snap rate, 66.7% of the rushing work, and a 54.3% route share (7.1% target share). During that span, he has averaged 18.6 touches with 78.7 total yards as the RB39 in fantasy points per game. The big problem continues to be his lack of touchdowns, as he has zero during that stretch. Among 45 qualifying rushers, he is 20th in explosive run rate and 23rd in missed tackle rate. Is this the Woody Marks breakout week? We shall see, but he has a wonderful matchup this week. Over their last five games, the Browns' run defense continues to stink, allowing the second-highest explosive run rate, the fifth-most yards after contact per attempt, and the second-highest missed tackle rate.

Cam Skattebo will be back this week (hamstring). He practiced in full on Tuesday and Wednesday. He doesn't carry an injury designation into Week 10. The last time we saw Skattebo, he was racking up 18 touches and 121 total yards against the Texans as the RB7 for the week. In that game, he had a 55.4% snap rate, 50% of the rushing work, and a 32.3% route share. I expect him to see a similar workload (if not elevated) this week. Among 45 qualifying backs, Skattebo is 17th in yards after contact per attempt and 11th in missed tackle rate. Skattebo is a volume-based RB2 this week with a tough matchup. Over their last five games, Washington has allowed the eighth-lowest explosive run rate, the fifth-fewest yards after contact per attempt, and the sixth-lowest missed tackle rate.

Last week, Ashton Jeanty took back the lead back duties with a 66% snap rate, 40% of the rushing work, and a 62.5% route share. Jeanty finished with 11 touches and 20 total yards. The Raiders' offensive line has been a limited factor for Jeanty and this ground game all season. The Raiders' offensive line remains dead last in yards before contact per attempt. Jeanty has managed only 2.18 yards after contact per attempt and a 12% missed tackle rate this season. Jeanty is only a low-end RB2/flex this week. Seattle remains a top-tier run defense. Over their last five games, Seattle has allowed the third-lowest explosive run rate, the third-fewest rushing yards over expectation per attempt, and the eighth-lowest missed tackle rate.

Since Week 5, Blake Corum has been the RB16 in fantasy points per game, averaging 11.8 touches and 72.8 total yards. He has scored a touchdown in each game, which has helped to prop up the limited volume and hyper-efficiency. Among 45 qualifying backs, Corum is fourth in explosive run rate and 14th in missed tackle rate. Corum could see his hot streak come to an end this week, but the Rams could feed him more volume this week as Kyren Williams and Corum could be the engines of the offense. Over their last five games, Arizona's run defense has tightened up, allowing the ninth-lowest explosive run rate, the 12th-lowest rushing success rate, and ranking 15th in yards before contact per attempt.

Corey Kiner will assume the lead back duties for New England. Last week, in the fourth quarter, Kiner played 52.9% of the snaps with 87.5% of the rushing work, and zero routes. During this quarter, Lan Larison was also involved, but he only had one route with a 47.1% snap rate (one carry). Larison will contribute on passing downs this week, but I expect Kiner to lead the way in snaps and rushing attempts. Kiner has been impressive with his limited touches, with a 14.9% explosive run rate, 2.48 yards after contact per attempt, and a 30% missed tackle rate. Kiner will need all the volume he can get and a score this week to pay off for fantasy. Detroit's run defense has been nasty lately. Over their last five games, they have allowed the fourth-lowest rushing success rate, the tenth-lowest rushing yards over expectation per attempt, and the second-lowest yards after contact per attempt.

Since Week 6, Rachaad White has been the RB25 in fantasy points per game, averaging 11 touches and 62 total yards. In those games, he has had a 57.4% snap rate, 40.3% of the rushing work, and a 40.2% route share (10.6% target share). Among 45 qualifying rushers, White is 32nd in yards after contact per attempt and 13th in missed tackle rate. White is a volume-based RB2/3 this week against an improved Giants' run defense. Over their last five games, New York has allowed the ninth-lowest rushing success rate, the 13th-lowest yards after contact per attempt, and the second-lowest missed tackle rate.

Quinshon Judkins is the RB25 in fantasy points per game, but he has been losing work to Dylan Sampson since Week 7. Over his last three games, he has averaged 15.6 touches and 66 total yards with a 42% snap rate, 55.1% of the rushing work, and a 16% route share. He has been primarily the early-down grinder, with Sampson handling passing downs and eating into his carry share. Judkins also continues to be inefficient with his rushing work. Among 45 qualifying rushers, he is 37th in explosive run rate, 39th in yards after contact per attempt, and 34th in missed tackle rate. Judkins could see a bump in these numbers this week. Houston's run defense has softened some recently. Over their last five games, Houston has allowed the third-highest rushing success rate, the ninth-most yards after contact per attempt, and the sixth-highest missed tackle rate. With his lack of passing game involvement, Judkins still likely needs a touchdown to pay off in fantasy this week.

Last week, Alvin Kamara didn't see his role grow as he operated as the passing-down back almost exclusively. Kamara had a 48.6% snap rate with only 18.8% of the rushing work, a 57.8% route share, and an 11.4% target share. Kamara finished with nine touches and 49 total yards (zero touchdowns). Kamara is only a middling PPR flex this week. Over their last five games, Carolina has allowed the fifth-fewest yards per target and the 14th-fewest receiving fantasy points per game to backs.

Last week, Audric Estime took over the "Kendre Miller role" in the Saints offense as the primary early down thumper. Estime had a 48.6% snap rate, 46.9% of the rushing work, and a 28.9% route share (2.9% target share). Estime handled all three of the red zone rushing attempts as he scored a touchdown. Estime was the RB10 for the week as he finished with 16 touches and 77 total yards. Estime has 2.08 yards after contact per attempt and a 13% missed tackle rate. Estime is a solid flex again this week. Over their last five games, Carolina has allowed the 14th-highest rushing success rate, the eighth-highest yards before contact per attempt, and the fifth-highest missed tackle rate.

Since Week 7, Rico Dowdle has been the RB23 in fantasy points per game, averaging 15 touches and 71 total yards. In those two games, Dowdle has had a 45.9% snap rate, a 38.1% rushing share, and a 45% route share (10.9% target share). Among 51 qualifying backs, Dowdle is 11th in yards after contact per attempt and 29th in missed tackle rate. Dowdle is a strong flex at his floor, but he could easily be an RB2 again this week. Over their last five games, Cincy has allowed the third-highest explosive run rate, the fourth-highest rushing success rate, and the seventh-highest yards after contact per attempt.

Since Jordan Mason's return, Aaron Jones has taken a step back with a 32.9% snap rate, a 30.5% rushing share, and a 22.9% route share. He has averaged only 7.3 touches and 29 total yards. Unless his role changes this week, this will be the last week that Jones is a must-write-up for the Primer, as he is just a change of pace/back up option for Minnesota right now. Jones is a low-end flex option this week, though. Over their last five games, Green Bay has allowed the 13th-highest rushing success rate, the sixth-most yards after contact per attempt, and the highest missed tackle rate.

Last week, Braelon Allen led the Jets' backfield in snap rate (58.1%) while seeing only a 32% rushing share, but he led the backfield in route share (39.5%). Allen was behind Breece Hall in opportunities, though. Allen finished with ten touches and 54 total yards. Hall had two red zone rushing attempts to Braelon Allen's one. Allen could see his workload take a step back this week with Hall another week away from his original injury. Allen is an RB3 who could post flex production if he gets in the end zone. Over their last five games, Buffalo has allowed the 13th-lowest rushing success rate and the 11th-lowest yards after contact per attempt while ranking 15th in rushing yards over expectation per attempt and explosive run rate.

Over the last three games, Jordan Mason has taken over as Minny's lead back with a 46.7% snap rate, a 49.2% rushing share, and a 29.2% route share (5.9% target share). He has averaged 10.4 touches and 43.3 total yards. Mason has a strong 14.3% explosive run rate and a decent 2.02 yards after contact per attempt. He could return low-end RB2/solid flex numbers this week. Over their last five games, Green Bay has allowed the 13th-highest rushing success rate, the sixth-most yards after contact per attempt, and the highest missed tackle rate.

Since Week 7, Dylan Sampson has had a 55.5% snap rate, 19.2% of the rushing work, and a 52.7% route share (11.1% target share). Sampson has averaged nine touches and 64.3 total yards as the RB36 in fantasy points per game. Sampson has 2.13 yards after contact per attempt and a 13% missed tackle rate. Neither of those marks are impressive. He can still be a decent flex this week in PPR formats. Over their last five games, Houston is tied for the most receiving touchdowns allowed to running backs while also surrendering the seventh-most receiving fantasy points per game to the position.

Omarion Hampton is the RB44 in fantasy points per game, averaging 14.2 touches and 54 total yards. Hampton hasn't scored a touchdown since Week 4. He has a 43% snap rate, a 45.5% rushing workload, and a 22.2% route share. Hampton has managed only 2.24 yards after contact per attempt and a 13% missed tackle rate. Hampton is a sit again this week. Over their last five games, Baltimore has allowed the second-lowest explosive run rate, the eighth-lowest rushing success rate, and the sixth-lowest yards after contact per attempt.

Last week, Kaleb Johnson finished with 14 carries, 68 yards on the ground, and a score. I expect him to be the early-down option for Green Bay's committee backfield. Johnson has been awesome on a per-touch basis this season with 2.83 yards after contact per attempt and a 26% missed tackle rate. The Green Bay offensive line has only managed to generate 1.26 yards before contact per attempt for him, though. I don't expect that number to be higher this week, but if he can find a crease, he could do some damage against this Minny run defense. Over their last five games, Minnesota has allowed the tenth-highest explosive run rate, the most yards after contact per attempt, and the fourth-highest missed tackle rate. Johnson could be a decent flex option this week.

Over the last two games, Kaelon Black has averaged 11.5 rushing attempts and 66.5 rushing yards while logging a 35.3% snap rate. He could easily see 10-12 touches again this week as a decent flex play. Black is a touchdown-dependent flex. He has almost no passing game role with only six targets this season. Black has posted a solid 2.43 yards after contact per attempt and a 15% missed tackle rate. Over their last five games, Dallas has allowed the 14th-highest explosive run rate, the second-most rushing yards over expectation per attempt, and the fourth-most yards after contact per attempt.

Chris Rodriguez is a viable flex option again this week. Rodriguez has 12 red zone carries this season while averaging 7.4 touches and 33 total yards. If he gets into the end zone this week, he could give you a comfy double-digit PPR points. Rodriguez has posted 2.20 yards after contact per attempt and an 18% missed tackle rate this season. The Titans' run defense has been giving. Over their last five games, they have allowed the sixth-highest explosive run rate, the fifth-highest rushing success rate, and the fifth-most yards before contact per attempt.

Emmett Johnson could turn in flex-worthy numbers this week. Over the last two games, he has gotten in the end zone in each game while averaging six touches and 88.5 total yards. Johnson has been incredible with his limited workload, with an astounding 3.27 yards after contact per attempt and a 35% missed tackle rate. The Falcons have had a Swiss cheese run defense. Over their last five games, Atlanta has allowed the highest explosive run rate, the seventh-highest rushing success rate, and the third-most yards after contact per attempt. Johnson could see 10-12 touches this week if Kansas City wants to lean on their ground game more with Patrick Mahomes playing through an injury.

MarShawn Lloyd missed last week's game with a knee issue. He opened this week not on the injury report. Zoom out to the entire season, and they have allowed the third-most yards per target and the fourth-most fantasy points per opportunity to the position. Mumpfield is a decent flex this week with a wonderful matchup. My biggest concerns for Mumpfield are his ability to earn a higher target share and Matthew Stafford's passing volume.
